subject: Streamline feasibility — performance, cost, quality alignment
messages:
From: Diego Fernandez <diego.fernandez@redwood.ai>
To: Lucia Ramos <lucia@streamline.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 26 Nov 2026 15:22:00 -0800
Subject: Streamline feasibility — performance, cost, quality alignment

Hi Lucia — thanks again for the call earlier. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we stay aligned before the kickoff: 

Summary of ask
- Streamline wants to validate a retrieval-augmented generation flow for realtime customer responses (search + answer synthesis).
- Target production-like workload: ~150–250 QPS at peak; 1–3k tokens per request average after chaining.

Draft success criteria (Redwood proposal) — please confirm these are sensible for Streamline: 
1) Performance: 95th pct latency across generation pipeline (end-to-end request -> first token) < 350ms at 150 QPS sustained; tail SLOs documented for 250 QPS burst.
2) Throughput: ability to sustain steady-state 150 QPS with <5% error rate; auto-scale to handle 250 QPS bursts.
3) Cost: target amortized cost/token <= $0.0009 (including caching & batching).
4) Quality: automated eval pass-rate >= 82% on your rubric (we'll use your 120-case prompt set + 30 human blind evals).
5) Operational: KV cache hit-rate >= 30% for prefix reuse; reproducible metrics and dashboards shared within 48 hours of each test run.

Ownership (proposal)
- Streamline: provide representative sample traffic + rubric, primary contact Lucia.
- Redwood: Diego (trial config & runtime tuning), Rishi (SRE for infra/SLOs), Marissa (CS for onboarding and ops runbooks).

Deliverables & timeline (proposed)
- By Nov 30: Streamline shares sample traffic (1–2M tokens) + rubric + ACL for testing.
- Dec 3–4: Redwood runs smoke benchmark (latency + cost baseline) and returns baseline report.
- Dec 7: Alignment call to finalize measurement script and gating thresholds.
- Dec 10–17: Formal 1-week trial window with at least 3 steady-state runs.
- Dec 20: Readout and recommendation with cost/latency tradeoffs and next-step proposal.

Attachments: I attached a measurement template (Redwood) to capture the metrics above and a small guidance doc on sample-traffic formatting.

Could you confirm by EOD tomorrow that the proposed success criteria look reasonable and that you can share the sample traffic by Nov 30? If that works I’ll book the smoke benchmark window on Dec 3.

Thanks — Diego
Diego Fernandez
Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference

-----
Attachment: redwood-poc-measurement-template.xlsx (spreadsheet template for latency/throughput/cost/quality)
Attachment: streamline-sample-traffic.tar.gz (placeholder - actual upload to secure share)

From: Lucia Ramos <lucia@streamline.ai>
To: Diego Fernandez <diego.fernandez@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 27 Nov 2026 09:18:00 -0500
Subject: Re: Streamline feasibility — performance, cost, quality alignment

Thanks Diego — recap looks great and aligns with internal expectations. A few clarifications: 

- Latency: our internal goal is 95th < 300ms. Is that achievable without model quantization or will you need a quantized variant?
- Cost: $0.0009/token is our upper bound for this trial. We’d like both a baseline and an optimized run so we can see the delta.
- Quality: we’ll share a 150-case rubric plus 30 blind evals; can Redwood run the automated pass-rate and include the blind eval scaffolding?

We’ll upload sample traffic to the Drive link you provided by Nov 30 (we will anonymize PII). Lucia (cc’ing Platform team).

—Lucia
Lucia Ramos
Head of Platform | Streamline.ai

-----
(Attachment note: we will upload a 1.6M-token sample file to the shared drive)

From: Diego Fernandez <diego.fernandez@redwood.ai>
To: Lucia Ramos <lucia@streamline.ai>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 27 Nov 2026 11:05:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Streamline feasibility — performance, cost, quality alignment

Thanks — helpful clarifications. Short answers: 
- Latency: baseline on the unquantized 13B-family is typically ~420ms 95p at 150 QPS; to hit 300ms we recommend either a tuned quantized variant or a smaller model + optimized KV caching. We’ll include both baseline and optimized runs in the December trial.
- Cost: we’ll produce two cost profiles (baseline + optimized) and show token-level breakdowns in the report.
- Quality: yes — we’ll run the automated rubric and manage the blind eval pipeline (will need 2–3 reviewers on your side for the blind set).

Action items updated: 
- Lucia: upload anonymized sample traffic and rubric by Nov 30.
- Diego/Rishi: run smoke benchmark Dec 3–4; share baseline report Dec 6.
- Marissa: prepare onboarding runbook and coordinate blind-eval logistics (Marissa will follow up with required reviewer counts).

I’ll schedule the Dec 7 alignment call once we have the sample set.

Diego

Quick infra note from Rishi — copying the proposed acceptance thresholds into infra actions: 

- Baseline cluster config will be provisioned on Dedicated nodes in us-west2. We will run the smoke benchmark on Dec 3; please expect temporary IP whitelisting requests for your upload.
- For latency target: we’ll run two paths — (A) unquantized model on an optimized kernel path (to get baseline) and (B) quantized 4-bit variant to show the latency/cost tradeoff. If Streamline can tolerate the quantized variation slightly degrading some edge-case quality we can hit the 300ms 95p target.
- Instrumentation: Diego & Marissa — we’ll need the evaluation script (entry point + metrics output schema) by Dec 2 so SRE can hook the dashboards.

Rishi
